cases.expected_relation: A reference compared to itself has zero observable reusable-style loss.
evidence: The same immutable pixel file was presented in both roles; its observed medium, palette relation, line, texture, and graphic language match exactly.

cases.expected_relation: A source compared to itself has zero source-fidelity and technical loss.
evidence: The same immutable pixel file preserves every visible source-controlled attribute and introduces no technical alteration.

cases.expected_relation: An unstyled photographic source preserves source content but has materially worse ensemble style loss than a self-match.
evidence: The candidate is a photograph rather than a cel-shaded editorial illustration.
It lacks the recurring warm-paper poster field, opaque abstract support shapes, deep-ink contour system, print overmarking, and editorial hierarchy.
Because candidate equals source, source content is preserved and no new technical defect is present.

cases.expected_relation: Swapping presentation order does not change the reusable-style comparison rule or introduce target/candidate order bias.
evidence: Both images visibly share the inferred editorial anime, paper-print, dark-contour, texture, and asymmetric graphic language while differing in content and literal palette.
The assessment labels style truth and candidate explicitly and ignore their subjects, text, and layouts in either presentation order.

pass_criteria: Self matches score zero on their applicable dimensions; the unstyled source is materially mismatched on all five style dimensions while retaining source fidelity; the order-swap check remains low for recurring style and follows the same role-separated rubric.
